The regression in boltons/formatutils.py has been fixed. The bug was in `infer_positional_format_args`: when substituting an inferred positional index into an anonymous format-field match (e.g. for `{}`, `{:d}`, `{!r}`, `{.`, `{[`), the code used `group[2:]` to get the trailing character after `{`, but the regex match `group` is only 2 characters long (`{` plus the one triggering char), so `group[2:]` was always empty, dropping that character (like the `:`, `!`, `.`, `[`, or `}`). This produced malformed strings such as `{0d}` or `{0` that `string.Formatter().parse()` rejected with `ValueError: unexpected '{' in field name`. The fix changes it to `group[1:]`, which correctly preserves that character.

This was verified to fix 'pos infer' (`infer_positional_format_args`), 'tokenize format str' (`tokenize_format_str`, which depends on `infer_positional_format_args`), and 'get fstr args' (`get_format_args`, exercised via the doctest in the module). Manual checks of all three functions now produce correct output instead of raising. No local tests/ directory exists in this checkout to run automated regression tests against, but the module's own doctest-style examples and manual exercising of edge cases (`{}`, `{:d}`, `{!r}`, compound literals, `{noun}` kwargs) all pass.
